$doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for `items.schema_ref` in the shared impress-core store.
The store matches `schema_ref` by EXACT EQUALITY (crates/impress-core/src/sql_query.rs).
No version tolerance, no namespace fallback, no fuzzy match. A reader that spells a
ref differently from its writer returns ZERO ROWS forever, silently, on every platform.
That failure mode is indistinguishable from 'the user has no data yet', which is why it
has shipped repeatedly and survived both code review and CI.
THE RULE: one canonical spelling per record kind, listed once here. Every schema-ref
string literal in the tree (Rust and Swift) must equal one of these. Enforced by
scripts/check-schema-refs.sh (call sites, suite-wide) and crates/*/tests/schema_ref_manifest.rs
(registry parity, both directions, per crate).
THERE IS NO NAMING CONVENTION TO INFER. Bare (`manuscript`), namespaced (`imbib/library`,
`core/operation`) and versioned (`task@1.0.0`) spellings all exist and all are correct for
their kind. Do not 'regularise' a ref by pattern-matching on its neighbours — that is the
exact reasoning that produced `manuscript-section@1.0.0` and `citation-usage@1.0.0`.
Copy the spelling from this file, not from a sibling call site.
`knownDivergences` is EMPTY and its budget is 0, as of WP C4. It held three entries:
the task and agent-run spelling splits (three live spellings each) and the dead
`impress/operation` registration. All three are resolved — the code by aligning every
writer, reader and registry, and the DATA by
`impress_core::task_schema_migration` (flagged off, dry-run first, reversible via a
changed-id ledger in `store_metadata`). The budget is a RATCHET: it may only shrink.
At 0, adding a divergence means raising the budget in the same change, in writing,
with the owner decision that made a second spelling of one kind acceptable.

canonical.ai-import-ledger@1.0.0: impress-core AI schemas. One atomic, content-hashed receipt per imported legacy LocalModels conversation; written by impress-ai so migration is restart-safe and changed source rows are surfaced instead of silently duplicated.
canonical.agent-run@1.0.0: VERSIONED, and the ONLY spelling of this kind since WP C4. Written by impel-core task_store AGENT_RUN_SCHEMA, by impel SharedTaskBridge.agentRoundCompleted, and by impress-ai AiStore.record_run_start (whose rows also carry available_tools — the ACTUAL tool surface shown to the model, beside the policy-declared enabled_tools). Rows also carry `executor_kind` (deterministic | model): `model` is NOT always an LLM — keyword tables and API pipelines record their algorithm there, and without this field `heuristic-v1` reads exactly like an inference call in every surface; registered ONCE, in impress-core schemas/task.rs (impel-core's register_impel_schemas delegates there); claimed by the AgentRunRecordKind descriptor, which is what AgentStoreReader and the agentRunsAll sidebar count read. The retired `agent-run` (impress-core registration, unwritten) and `impel/agent-run` (SharedTaskBridge) rows are converged by impress_core::task_schema_migration.
canonical.annotation: impress-core. Written by imbib annotation sync.

Kept in `canonical` rather than moved to `registeredButUnwritten` because reclassifying it would reject existing call sites and belongs to the imbib pass, not C4's. This note used to say 'see registeredButUnwritten', which held only `impress/operation` and is now empty.

canonical.content-blob@1.0.0: impress-core AI schemas. Immutable content-addressed metadata for multimodal bytes; written by impress-ai. Bytes live behind the BlobStore port, never inline in payload_json.
canonical.content-chunk@1.0.0: impress-core source schemas. Domain-neutral text derived from immutable source bytes, pinned to an extraction run and structured source locator.
canonical.conversation@1.0.0: impress-core AI schemas. Durable research conversation parent; written and read by impress-ai and intended for impart macOS/iOS presentation.
canonical.core/operation: The operation journal / CRDT log. Written and queried by impress-core sqlite_store; its one schema definition lives in imbib-core unified::schemas::core_operation_schema. NOT `impress/operation`: impress-core registered that id from the start and nothing ever wrote or read it — the dead registration (schemas/operation.rs) was deleted in WP C4. Remaining wart, deliberately not fixed here: the WRITER crate (impress-core) registers no definition for this id, so registry.validate() is a no-op for operation rows in an impress-core-only registry. Moving the definition up from imbib-core is the fix and is out of C4's boundary.
canonical.core/verb-call@1.0.0: VERSIONED, beside `core/operation` it joins (ADR-0036 D2, plan-self-reflective-layer D-R1/D-R2, plan-verb-pipeline P2). One row per NON-READ-ONLY verb call on EVERY path (MCP, CLI, surface, FFI, impel, ai-tools): the verb, the caller identity the pipeline established from the transport (never an argument), trace and parent ids, a privacy-filtered argument summary (ids and short scalars by value; long strings as length + sha256_8; objects as keys), outcome, duration. The row's id IS the call id, and every `core/operation` row the verb wrote carries it as `batch_id` (stamped by sqlite_store from the task-local call context), so `ops_for(item) -> batch_id -> call` answers 'why did this change'. Registered in impress-core schemas/verb_call.rs (VERB_CALL_SCHEMA); written ONLY by impress-store-service's audit sink (the pipeline's audit layer hands it a record; a bounded channel and one writer thread). Not an operation (D-R2: an op needs one target; a call has zero or many). Compactable, Private, never synced; read-only calls are not recorded unless IMPRESS_CALL_LOG=all.
canonical.dataset: impress-core (implore schemas). Written by implore ImploreStoreAdapter.
canonical.extraction-run@1.0.0: impress-core source schemas. Reproducibility record for text, OCR, layout, table, or figure extraction; written by domain ingestion adapters.
canonical.figure: impress-core (implore schemas). Written by implore ImploreStoreAdapter.
canonical.imbib/bibliography-entry: imbib-core. THE publication ref. Written by imbib-core conversion.rs:113. Reading bare `bibliography-entry` is the iOS-citation-picker bug. Also the impel enrichment spawn trigger (impel-enrichment BIBLIOGRAPHY_ENTRY_SCHEMA, scanned by impel-taskd): that constant read `bibliography-entry@1.0.0` until 2026-07-29, so the pipeline matched zero rows and never spawned a task — fixed, and pinned against this writer by `enrichment_trigger_matches_the_ref_imbib_actually_writes`.
canonical.imbib/eink-device: imbib-core. One e-ink tablet imbib mirrors papers to (transport, mirror mode, folder options, import options). Written only by ImbibStore::eink_configure_device and the mirror engine's per-sync stamps (crates/imbib-core/src/eink/store.rs).
canonical.imbib/eink-mirror: imbib-core. One publication's presence on one e-ink device (state, remote id/parent/name, uploaded sha, import stamps); parent = the bibliography-entry. Written only by the mirror engine (crates/imbib-core/src/eink/store.rs).
canonical.mail-account: impress-core. Written by impart ImpartStoreAdapter, and (fixtures only) by impress-iOS ImpressIOSUITestSeed, which takes the spelling from here rather than from a sibling call site.
canonical.mail-folder: impress-core. Written by impart ImpartStoreAdapter, and (fixtures only) by impress-iOS ImpressIOSUITestSeed.
canonical.manuscript: impress-core + imbib-core. Written by imprint ManuscriptStoreAdapter, impel JournalPipeline. ADR-0023 W3 added the OPTIONAL payload field `external_source` (JSON: path + content_hash + state present|missing + watched-file/folder refs). Present ⇒ the row is a REFERENCE-IN-PLACE index entry: the FILE is authoritative for the body, `body_content` is a snapshot replaced on every re-read, the row takes no editor session, and nothing writes the file back (D4). Written by imprint ManuscriptStoreAdapter.upsertExternalManuscript. Do NOT confuse with `import_source`, which asserts the opposite (a copy was taken; the original is detached). The schema ref itself is unchanged and kind_scope stays `manuscript`.
canonical.manuscript-collection: impress-core + imbib-core. Manuscript folder envelope; written by imprint ManuscriptMigrationRunner.
canonical.manuscript-revision: impress-core + imbib-core. Written by impel JournalSnapshotJob.
canonical.manuscript-section: impress-core + imbib-core. Written BARE by imprint ImprintStoreAdapter.syncSections (Swift, gated on hasThroughline) and crates/imprint-service/src/sections.rs SECTION_SCHEMA_REF (Rust, app-closed/MCP path). Reading `manuscript-section@1.0.0` was the outline/sections/cross-doc-search bug.
canonical.memory/claim@1.0.0: VERSIONED. Suite-scoped memory claim — what is true (ADR-0028 memory kernel, knowledge-object convention per ADR-0012 D39). Registered in impress-core schemas/memory.rs (MEMORY_CLAIM_SCHEMA) next to the impress_core::memory_ops kernel that writes it. Written by impress-memory-service MemoryService::remember and the impel-memory consolidation executor, both of which go through memory_ops::insert_memory_item; read by the memory recall/brief surfaces (memory_ops::recall / memory_ops::brief) and by whatever agent prompt those feed. `title` + `body` are spelled exactly so because they are the two items_fts columns — memory is searchable with zero sqlite_store changes. Replacement is a Supersedes edge (D39 rule 5), never an in-place edit, so a superseded claim stays in the graph for audit.
canonical.memory/episode@1.0.0: VERSIONED. Suite-scoped memory episode — what happened, with task_kind/approach/outcome/quality so "how did this kind of task go last time?" is a query rather than a transcript re-read (ADR-0028 memory kernel, ADR-0012 D39). Registered in impress-core schemas/memory.rs (MEMORY_EPISODE_SCHEMA). Written by impress-memory-service MemoryService::remember and the impel-memory consolidation executor via memory_ops::insert_memory_item; read by memory_ops::recall / memory_ops::brief.
canonical.memory/instruction@1.0.0: VERSIONED. Suite-scoped standing instruction — what to do, from the user (ADR-0028 memory kernel, ADR-0012 D39). Registered in impress-core schemas/memory.rs (MEMORY_INSTRUCTION_SCHEMA). Written by impress-memory-service MemoryService::remember and the impel-memory consolidation executor via memory_ops::insert_memory_item; read by memory_ops::recall and led by memory_ops::brief, whose first section is instructions. `rule` absent means `body` IS the rule. Retired ONLY by supersession or the no_recall flag — never by an agent deciding it no longer applies.
canonical.provider@1.0.0: VERSIONED (ADR-0034 D-P4, plan-verb-pipeline P8). Local runtime provider registration and trust, registered in impress-core schemas/provider.rs and written only by impress-store-service providers.rs. The row stores validated descriptor JSON and the SHA-256 hash of a host-issued rotated credential, NEVER the raw token; the token is a private 0600 hash-addressed file in this workspace. This schema is excluded from the sync outbox: provider endpoints, credentials, and trust are local to one host.
canonical.review: impress-core knowledge objects. Written by impel JournalReviewService.
canonical.review-request@1.0.0: VERSIONED, and in NO registry. Written by impel-core task_store REVIEW_REQUEST_SCHEMA (open_review) and RESOLVED by three writers: imbib RustStoreAdapter.resolveReview + imprint ThroughlineCoordinator.resolveProposal (both via impress-store-ffi resolve_review, which validates the schema and attributes resolved_by) and impel-taskd's hourly expiry sweep (resolution='expired' after IMPEL_REVIEW_EXPIRY_DAYS, default 7). Read by imbib RustStoreAdapter listPendingReviews/countPendingReviews (the review queue + badge — BOTH page through the full population; a newest-500 window once made older reviews permanently unapprovable), imprint ThroughlineCoordinator.pendingProposals (same full paging), and impel-core reviews_for/unresolved_review_targets (the scheduler's suspension set). Canonical because it is genuinely the written spelling; the missing registration is tracked in registeredButUnwritten's inverse and is why registry.validate() is a no-op for these rows.
canonical.revision-note: impress-core knowledge objects. Written by impel JournalReviewService.
canonical.source-citation@1.0.0: impress-core source schemas. Immutable-byte-pinned structured citation with page, region, range, section, figure, and table location; written by curation and ingestion adapters.
canonical.task@1.0.0: VERSIONED, and the ONLY spelling of this kind since WP C4. Selected by impress-core sqlite_store ready_tasks — which is why it won: it is the spelling with a live queue behind it, so converging on it means nothing that is scheduled today stops being scheduled. Written by impel-core task_spawn TASK_SCHEMA, by impel SharedTaskBridge.taskCreated, and by impress-ai AiStore (queue_user_turn `impress.ai.respond` and queue_title_suggestion `impress.ai.suggest-title` — both carry task_kind, so ready_tasks schedules them); registered ONCE, in impress-core schemas/task.rs, whose fields are the union of the writers' payloads (incl. `next_attempt_at`, the retry-backoff not-before that ready_tasks honors, and `spawned_by`, the SpawnRule that CREATED the task — `assigned_to` names only the executor that later ran it); inherited by manuscript-submission; claimed by the TaskRecordKind descriptor, which is what AgentStoreReader and the agentTasksAll sidebar counts read. TWO STATE VOCABULARIES coexist in rows: the kernel writes pending/running/done/failed/cancelled, the bridge writes queued/completed — bridged by TaskState::parse_compat in Rust and by AgentStoreReader.stateSpellings + ImpelStoreAdapter.threadState on the Swift readers (an exact single-spelling payloadEq once made every kernel task invisible to its sidebar state child). The retired `task` (impress-core registration, unwritten in production) and `impel/task` (SharedTaskBridge) rows are converged by impress_core::task_schema_migration. NOTE: ready_tasks additionally requires a non-empty payload `task_kind`, so bridge-MIRRORED rows converge without becoming schedulable.
canonical.task-event@1.0.0: VERSIONED, like `task@1.0.0` it belongs to (ADR-0034 D6, plan P4). One row per progress event of a JOB — a long-running verb that answered with a `task@1.0.0` handle — PRUNED TO THE LAST 200 rows per task: the surface event ring's shape (`seq` gap-free and derived into the row id, cursor from the rows read, `gap` when pruned past the cursor) applied to a task. Registered in impress-core schemas/task.rs (TASK_EVENT_SCHEMA) beside the task it annotates; written and read ONLY by impress-core job.rs (append_event / events_after), which the inline runner (impress-store-service job.rs) and the `impel-service_job-events` / `job-wait` verbs go through. Ephemeral like the surface ring: Private, never synced, pruned not archived — a job's durable record is its task row (`state`, `result`, `error`) and whatever rows the verb itself wrote.
canonical.figure-region@1.0.0: VERSIONED. PDF figure/image region provenance for vw knowledge ingest (9aec0265). Registered in impress-core schemas/source.rs (FIGURE_REGION_SCHEMA); written AND read exclusively through impress-store-service source_service.rs via that same constant, so writer and readers cannot drift. Added to the manifest one commit late — the schema-refs pre-push gate caught the omission.
canonical.tool-invocation@1.0.0: impress-core AI schemas. One attributed SciX, Impress MCP, web, or other tool call made during an agent/model run; written by impress-ai.
canonical.vw/command-receipt@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Durable idempotency receipt keyed from a caller command UUID and containing the original typed session result.
canonical.vw/configuration@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Exact vehicle configuration and deviations used for knowledge applicability.
canonical.vw/diagnostic-session@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Persistent VW diagnostic aggregate pinned to a knowledge-pack and deterministic-engine version.
canonical.vw/knowledge-pack@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Immutable curated VW knowledge-pack manifest and typed content.
canonical.vw/measurement@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Queryable child measurement with unit, acquisition context, and parent diagnostic session.
canonical.vw/observation@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Queryable child observation with acquisition context and supersession history.
canonical.vw/photo-evidence@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Private, hash-pinned user photo evidence ingested from an authorized ChatGPT file handoff and linked to the generic media artifact, content blob, and optional diagnostic session.
canonical.vw/procedure-run@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Durable execution state for a published diagnostic procedure.
canonical.vw/vehicle@1.0.0: vw-impress-adapter. Vehicle identity linked to its exact configuration.
canonical.watched-file@1.0.0: VERSIONED. impress-core schemas/watched_folder.rs (ADR-0023 D4). One row per file a watched folder has ever discovered — an INDEX ENTRY, never a copy: path, sha256 content hash, mtime, and a `state` of present|missing. Written and read ONLY by impress-store-service DocsImportService (import_discovered / finish_watched_scan / record_produced_rows / list_watched_files), which is the single writer for both ingest units. A vanished file's row is marked `missing`, never deleted, because the rows it produced are still real. `produced_ids` is the W2 seam: discovery leaves it absent and the app's real importer fills it in through record_produced_rows.
canonical.watched-folder@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0023 D2 names it. impress-core schemas/watched_folder.rs. One row per folder the user (or an agent, via MCP/CLI) asked the suite to watch: path + optional security-scoped bookmark, kind_scope, enabled, declared volume_state (D6) and last-scan stats. Written by impress-store-service DocsImportService add_watched_folder / update_watched_folder / finish_watched_scan; W1's Swift FolderWatchService reaches it through those verbs, never with its own writer. The watched file TYPES and the ingest UNIT are deliberately NOT fields here — they are derived from the record kind's FileDiscoveryCapability (D1), which is the one authority for both.
canonical.manuscript-change@1.0.0: impress-core collab (ADR-0027). One IMMUTABLE chunk of Automerge changes for a manuscript body — kind "change" (one commit's raw changes) or "snapshot" (a full save written by compaction). Envelope parent = the manuscript (the load query is HasParent). Written ONLY by impress-core collab.rs; read by the same; compacted by the AI daemon's cycle. Registered once in impress-core schemas/manuscript_change.rs (MANUSCRIPT_CHANGE_SCHEMA_REF).
canonical.manuscript-file@1.0.0: VERSIONED. impress-core schemas/manuscript_file.rs (ADR-0030 D1). One row per file of a manuscript's project tree EXCEPT the entry — the entry's text is the manuscript row's `body_content`, so a manuscript with no file rows is a one-file project and nothing migrates. Envelope parent = the manuscript (HasParent lists the tree; delete cascades). Id = uuid_v5(MANUSCRIPT_FILE_ID_NAMESPACE, "<manuscript>|<path>"), so `get_file` is one get and a re-import mints the same row. Text at or below INLINE_TEXT_LIMIT is inline in `content` and Automerge-backed through collab.rs (TextFields: content/content_hash/modified_ms); binaries and larger text are `blob:sha256:` refs into the workspace CAS (impress-core blobs, `<workspace>/content`). Written ONLY by impress-core manuscript_project.rs (put_file / move_file / set_file_field / record_derived) and by collab.rs materialize_body for inline text; read by the same, by imprint-core's project engine through load_project, and by the imprint-project-service verbs.
canonical.manuscript-build@1.0.0: VERSIONED. impress-core schemas/manuscript_build.rs (ADR-0030 D8). One row per EXPLICIT build of a manuscript project (⌘B, project-build, snapshot, export) — never a preview compile, which would be a churn incident. Envelope parent = the manuscript. Carries the target, engine, input stamp, outputs as blob refs, structured diagnostics in tree paths, the figure steps that ran, and whether shell steps were allowed. Written ONLY by impress-core manuscript_project.rs (record_build / finish_build); compacted to BUILD_RETENTION per manuscript by compact_builds / compact_all_builds (the daemon's hygiene cycle).
canonical.impress/scenario@1.0.0: VERSIONED (docs/plan-self-reflective-layer.md S1, § Scenarios; ask-first D-R1, approved). impress-core schemas/scenario.rs (SCENARIO_SCHEMA_REF) — one row per stored scenario: a starting state (`seed`), a sequence of `call`/`event`/`gesture`/`wait` steps, and expectations. The `spec` field is the whole `impress_scenario::Scenario`, stored verbatim as its own JSON TEXT (not a structural `Object`), one definition in crates/impress-scenario, the same discipline `impress/ui/surface@1.0.0`'s `spec` field documents. Written by impress-scenario-service's scenario-service_create/_update; read by _get/_list/_run. The three `run_selftest` verbs (imprint-selftest, impress-layout-service, impress-surface-service) run the scenarios stored under their own catalogue ids and keep their names (SC-1). Private + Durable; syncs like a named layout or surface — an authored scenario is a durable artifact, not scratch state.
canonical.impress/ui/layout@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0019 D1 and ADR-0031 D4 name it. impress-core schemas/ui.rs (LAYOUT_SCHEMA_REF) — one row per named or live workspace arrangement. The `layout` field is the whole tree: the serde JSON of `impress_layout::Layout` (windows over one tile arena, containers over panes, channel state), stored verbatim as open JSON so the shape has ONE definition, in crates/impress-layout, and not a flattened second copy here. Written by impress-layout-service (L3) — save_layout / apply_layout / commit, as Durable operations, with the Ephemeral drag-and-resize churn coalesced on release per ADR-0019 D6; read by the chassis layout projection (L6) and the ADR-0019 D5 importer (L7), which migrates `PaneLayoutState`, `imbib.layout.*` and the ⌃⌘1–9 layouts into these rows. SCOPE (ADR-0019 D2): a named layout (`name` set, `is_live` false) is Private + Durable and SYNCS to every device; the live arrangement (`name` null, `is_live` true) is Private + Durable too but carries `device`, so the projection filters it to the current machine instead of applying a 27" iMac's arrangement to a laptop. Geometry inside `layout.windows[].geometry` is device-scoped in EVERY case and must be filtered by the projection before a travelled layout is applied — the logical tree is what ports. Focus, selection and channel values are Ephemeral and never reach this row.
canonical.impress/ui/preset@1.0.0: VERSIONED. impress-core schemas/ui.rs (PRESET_SCHEMA_REF) — a shipped or user-edited preset, which under ADR-0031 D10 is what an app IS: a set of named queries (`queries`: name → PaneQuery JSON), a default tree (`layout`, same `impress_layout::Layout` JSON as the layout record), and a role assignment (`roles`: role → pane path or tile id). Required fields are `name` and `app_id` only; the other three are optional because a user-edited preset may override one facet and inherit the rest from the shipped preset it DerivedFrom, and `version` is the shipped revision so "the user edited Triage" is distinguishable from "we shipped a newer Triage". Written by impress-layout-service (L3) and seeded by the L7 preset importer; read by the chassis layout projection (L6) and the ADR-0019 D5 importer (L7). Presets are store records rather than Rust constants precisely so the developer stops making layout decisions for the user. Private + Durable; syncs.
canonical.impress/ui/surface@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0033 D1 names it. impress-core schemas/ui.rs (SURFACE_SCHEMA_REF) — one row per stored, declarative UI document: an agent builds a GUI for a Rust capability by writing one of these. The `spec` field is the whole `SurfaceSpec`, stored verbatim as its own JSON TEXT (not a structural `Object`, unlike `layout`) so the shape has ONE definition, in crates/impress-surface, and because a spec is read and authored as text by an agent (`surface_schema`, `surface_validate`, a chat transcript) as often as it is machine-parsed. Written by impress-surface-service (S4, ADR-0033 D4) — surface_create / surface_update; read by surface_get / surface_list and rendered by the `surface` view kind (S6/S7), which points a pane's query at `item(id)` of this kind so a surface obeys every ADR-0031 pane rule (parameters, channels, roles, undo, presets) with no special case. SCOPE (ADR-0019 D2 / ADR-0033 D5): Private + Durable, and SYNCS — a surface an agent built is a durable artifact of the conversation, like a named layout, not scratch state.
canonical.impress/ui/surface-state@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0033 D5 names it. impress-core schemas/ui.rs (SURFACE_STATE_SCHEMA_REF) — one row per `(surface, host)` pair: the working state a running instance of a surface has accumulated at its `state.*` paths, the JSON text `impress-surface::reduce` is the one function that writes. Written by impress-surface-service (S4) — surface_dispatch (a `field` change sets its `bind` path); read by surface_render, surface_state_get and the cross-process liveness poll (S5, ADR-0033 D6, `surface_wait` uses the same poll). SCOPE (ADR-0019 D2 / ADR-0033 D5): Ephemeral and device-scoped — `host` is the state instance and defaults to the device id: every pane on one device that shows a surface shares its one state row (and one runtime), which is also the row an agent reaches by leaving `host` out; a caller passes another `host` only for a private instance no pane shows (docs/agent-surfaces.md, `host`; review AC-F21). The layout verbs call the same value `device`. NEVER SYNCED: this row exists so an agent driving the suite from a separate process (impress-mcp) can read back what the human changed, not so anyone analyses it later.
canonical.impress/settings@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0036 D5 / plan-self-reflective-layer.md D-R1 name it. impress-core schemas/settings.rs (SETTINGS_SCHEMA_REF; `impress_settings::SYNCED_SCHEMA_REF` is pinned equal by test). ONE row per store: the `Synced` scope of the settings registry (`crates/impress-settings`), `values` = registry key → JSON value. Written and read ONLY by impress-store-service `settings_service::StoreSyncedBackend` (the `settings-service_set`/`reset` verbs for a synced key; deterministic UUIDv5 id from the ref). Every other scope (Device, App, Library) is a FILE under `<workspace>/settings/`, never a row, so a daemon or the CLI reads a port without opening the store. Private + Durable; syncs — that is the whole point of the row.
canonical.impress/ui/surface-event@1.0.0: VERSIONED, exactly as ADR-0033 D5 names it. impress-core schemas/ui.rs (SURFACE_EVENT_SCHEMA_REF) — one row per event a surface has emitted (a spec's `{ "emit": { name, payload } }` action, resolved by `impress-surface::reduce`'s effect list), PRUNED TO THE LAST 200 rows per `(surface, host)`. Written by impress-surface-service (S4) as part of surface_dispatch's effect execution; read by surface_events and long-polled by surface_wait(id, after_seq, timeout_ms) — "create → show → wait → update or act → wait" is the agent loop ADR-0033 D5 describes, and this row is what `wait` waits on. SCOPE (ADR-0019 D2 / ADR-0033 D5): Ephemeral, device-scoped like surface-state, NEVER SYNCED, and pruned for the same reason ADR-0031's privacy decision states: the standard build records nothing that exists only to be analysed later — the ring is pruned, not archived.
canonical.impress/workflow@1.0.0: VERSIONED (ask-first D-R1, plan-self-reflective-layer). impress-core schemas/workflow.rs (WORKFLOW_SCHEMA) — one row per stored, reviewable action sequence: a trigger (schedule | store | job | message | call | manual), guards, the surface's own params/sources/steps vocabulary (steps reuses impress_surface::spec::Action, never forked — WF-2), and review metadata (D-R6). Written by impress-store-service history_service.rs save_macro (state: "proposed", trigger: {"manual": {}}, steps built from named core/verb-call@1.0.0 rows) and by impress-workflow-service's workflow-service_create (W1); read and driven (validate/dry-run/enable/disable) by impress-workflow-service, over the pure crate impress-workflow's validator and planner. Running a workflow on its own trigger (a schedule tick, a store change, a finished job) is W2's planner in impel-taskd and the app's FFI tick, not this record's writer. Private + Durable; syncs, like a named layout — a workflow a person or an agent wrote is a durable artifact, not scratch state.

$registriesDoc: Exactly what each crate's schema-registration entry point produces. Asserted in BOTH
directions by crates/<crate>/tests/schema_ref_manifest.rs — a new, renamed or dropped
schema fails its crate's test until this list is updated in the same PR. Per-crate so
no new dependency edges are needed to make each direction total.
The same id may appear under two crates, but there is only ever ONE DEFINITION of it.
`task@1.0.0` / `agent-run@1.0.0` are defined in impress-core (schemas/task.rs, next to
the `ready_tasks` query that consumes them) and impel-core's entry point DELEGATES
there — it does not keep a copy. Two definitions of one id drift, which is exactly how
impel ended up with a registry saying `impel/task` while its kernel wrote `task@1.0.0`.
